# M0 Benchmark Harness

Purpose: measure Pixel 9 Pro Fold–class hardware performance for the models
Skein v1 will ship, so architectural decisions cite real numbers instead of
estimates.

**Deliverable:** `docs/MEASUREMENTS.md` at repo root, generated by
`lib/collect.py aggregate` and referenced from the design spec.

This harness was refactored to the **proven topology** established during
physical Fold provisioning — see
`docs/Handoffs/skein-fold-m0-hardware-handoff.md` for the full story. The
short version:

```text
Mac (this repo)
   |            |
  ADB          ADB-forwarded SSH
   |            |
GrapheneOS   Termux (u0_a214)
   |            +-- ~/skein-device/bin/  (pinned llama-bench/llama-cli)
   +-- thermal/battery/meminfo telemetry
```

- **ADB** talks to Android system state: device identity, thermal headroom,
  battery, and the shared-storage model files under `/sdcard/skein-bench/`.
- **SSH** (via `adb forward tcp:18022 tcp:8022` and the `skein-fold-agent`
  `~/.ssh/config` Host alias) reaches Termux's private storage, where the
  pinned `llama-bench` binaries actually live. ADB cannot read Termux-private
  files (`run-as com.termux` doesn't work — Termux isn't debuggable) — this
  split is intentional, not a workaround.
- The **Mac remains the orchestrator and result store**. Nothing analysis-
  or Git-related runs on the device.

## Frozen baseline

`output/baseline/` holds the frozen provisioning-day artifacts and is
**immutable** — never edit or overwrite these files. A deliberate
environment change gets a new dated file (`device-baseline-<date>.txt`),
never an edit to the original.

```text
output/baseline/device-baseline-2026-09-20.txt      — Android/CPU/toolchain fingerprint
output/baseline/llama-binaries-2026-09-20.sha256    — pinned binary hashes
```

`models.yaml`'s `binaries:` section carries copies of those hashes for
run.sh to check against at execution time; if they ever drift, that's a
manifest bug — fix `models.yaml`, never the baseline file.

## Quickstart

```bash
# Validate the whole pipeline with no Fold attached — mocks ADB/SSH,
# writes marker JSON, completes in well under 10s.
./run.sh --dry-run --smoke

# What the coordinator actually runs against the Fold: one CPU cell + one
# Vulkan cell on the Q3_K_M smoke artifact, loose thermal gate.
./run.sh --smoke

# Full formal matrix on the pinned Q4_K_M candidate (must be acquired and
# have its sha256 pinned in models.yaml first — see below). Strict thermal
# gate, >=3 repeats per cell.
./run.sh --formal

# Resume an interrupted formal matrix from the next uncompleted cell.
./run.sh --formal --resume
```

## Modes

| Flag         | Model                       | Backends       | Thermal gate | Repeats |
|--------------|------------------------------|-----------------|--------------|---------|
| `--smoke`    | Q3_K_M smoke artifact only   | cpu + vulkan     | loose (≤0.90 headroom) | 1 |
| `--formal`   | Q4_K_M candidate (pinned sha256 required) | cpu + vulkan | strict (≤0.50 headroom) | ≥3 |
| `--dry-run`  | combine with either mode above | — | — | — |
| `--resume`   | skip cells already recorded in `output/<date>/.state.json` | | | |

`--formal` refuses to run against any model whose `formal_m0_candidate` is
not `true` in `models.yaml` — this is how the Q3_K_M-is-smoke-only rule is
enforced in code, not just by convention. It also refuses to run if the
target model's `sha256` is still the `TBD` placeholder.

Other flags: `--model <id>`, `--backend cpu|vulkan`, `--context <N...>`
(space-separated, quote multiple values in one arg), `--repeats <N>`. See
`./run.sh --help`.

## Control flow (per cell)

```text
preflight (ADB device identity + skein-fold-agent SSH reachable + thermal envelope)
  -> verify binary SHA-256 over SSH (Termux-private) and model SHA-256 over ADB (shared storage)
  -> capture start thermal state via ADB
  -> start ADB/SSH telemetry sampler (thermal + battery + bench process RSS)
  -> SSH into Termux, invoke the selected llama-bench binary with --output json
  -> collect stdout/stderr for the cell
  -> stop the sampler; kill any orphan benchmark process in Termux
  -> capture end thermal state via ADB
  -> normalize + write output/<date>/<cell>/result.json on the Mac
  -> thermal cool-down gate before the next cell
```

Every cell — success, dry-run, or failure (OOM/timeout/thermal-abort) —
writes exactly one `result.json`. Failures are valid results with a
`failure_reason`; there are no silent retries.

## Layout

```text
tools/m0-benchmark/
├── README.md                 — this file
├── run.sh                    — Mac orchestrator (arg-driven; see Modes above)
├── models.yaml                — model + binary manifest (hashes, formal/smoke flags)
├── lib/
│   ├── common.sh              — logging + the one mockable adb/ssh choke point
│   ├── preflight.sh            — device identity, SSH reachability, hash/thermal checks
│   ├── thermal.sh              — thermal gate state machine (classify/gate/cooldown)
│   ├── telemetry.sh            — ADB/SSH sampler start/stop, PID resolution, orphan cleanup
│   ├── ssh-exec.sh             — llama-bench command-line building + remote execution
│   ├── models.py               — stdlib-only models.yaml reader (no PyYAML dependency)
│   └── collect.py              — JSON result schema, per-cell writer, MEASUREMENTS.md aggregator
├── prompts/                   — test prompts of varying lengths
│   ├── short-100t.txt
│   ├── medium-1k.txt
│   └── long-8k.txt
├── tests/                     — unit tests for every pure function (no Fold required)
│   ├── run-tests.sh
│   ├── assert.sh
│   ├── test_preflight.sh / test_thermal.sh / test_telemetry.sh / test_ssh_exec.sh
│   └── test_models.py / test_collect.py
└── output/
    ├── baseline/               — frozen provisioning artifacts (immutable, tracked in git)
    ├── dryrun/                 — --dry-run output (gitignored)
    └── <date>/                 — real run output, one dir per cell + .state.json (gitignored)
```

## JSON result schema

Every `result.json` (see `lib/collect.py:SCHEMA_FIELDS`) carries the full
provenance list from the handoff (§14):

```text
device_build_fingerprint, android_version, android_security_patch,
llama_cpp_commit, binary_sha256, model_sha256, model_quantization,
backend, cmdline, context_length, gpu_layers, threads, prompt_target,
gen_target, repeat_index, thermal_start, thermal_end, pp_toks_per_s,
tg_toks_per_s, ttft_ms, peak_rss_mb, battery_state, charging_state,
exit_status, timestamp_start, timestamp_end
```

plus `failure_reason` (present whenever `exit_status != 0`) and
`is_dry_run` (present and `true` only on `--dry-run` cells).

## Staged experiment sequence (handoff §19)

1. **Stage A — harness dry run.** `--dry-run --smoke`, then `--smoke` for
   real against the Fold: one CPU cell + one Vulkan cell on Q3_K_M. Proves
   the whole pipeline before anything formal.
2. **Stage B — formal artifact qualification.** Acquire the Q4_K_M
   candidate (skein-bxk), verify its SHA/source/license, pin it in
   `models.yaml`, tiny smoke on CPU and Vulkan.
3. **Stage C — backend baseline.** `--formal` at one context length,
   CPU vs Vulkan, identical prompt/gen targets and starting thermal state.
4. **Stage D — context/memory sweep.** `--formal --context "4096 8192
   16384"` before investing in 24K/32K.
5. **Stage E — sustained thermal run.** Longer generation against the
   chosen backend; watch `thermal_start`/`thermal_end` across repeats.
6. **Stage F — embedder/GLiNER measurements.** Separate harness work, after
   the LLM path here is stable.

## Aggregating results

```bash
python3 lib/collect.py aggregate output/<date> --report ../../docs/MEASUREMENTS.md
```

Every row in the generated report cites its source cell directory, so every
claim is auditable back to a `result.json`.

## Ground rules

- Every claim in `MEASUREMENTS.md` must trace to a `result.json` — no
  numbers without a matching file in `output/`.
- `--formal` requires ≥3 repeats per cell for statistical validity.
- The Fold should be plugged in and quiescent (screen off, no other apps)
  during formal runs; battery-mode runs are a separate, clearly labeled
  data set — never mixed into the same table as a plugged-in run.
- Only the dedicated hardware-runner agent executes this harness against
  the physical Fold — see `docs/DEVICE_RUNNER.md`.
